items.title: Phil Mead interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, June 1, 2006
items.q: I mean we were much more listening to the stuff that was going on in New York, so Turk Murphy and Kid Ory and stuff like that, not that we didn’t like it we just didn’t deal with that very much.

ctx.x: That’s a big event, isn’t it. That’s great.

But just to finish up one thing, so we didn’t think of ourselves in the Catatonic Five as playing traditional jazz. And we frankly didn’t listen to a lot of traditional jazz. I mean we were much more listening to the stuff that was going on in New York, so Turk Murphy and Kid Ory and stuff like that, not that we didn’t like it we just didn’t deal with that very much.

Right. I think it’s how musicians usually learn music is they grab what’s happening at the time and then if they get interested to go backwards they will. Like gee where did this come from, who do you suppose these people listened to.
